t: You're looking at the Grade II listed statue of John Stuart Mill, in the Temple Gardens on the Victoria Embankment. Mill was a philosopher and political economist, described as the most influential English-speaking philosopher of the nineteenth century. He argued for individual liberty against unlimited state and social control, and also for proportional representation and the emancipation of women. The sculptor was Thomas Woolner, a poet and one of the founding members of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood, and the only sculptor among its original members.
